items.title: Sheila Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Middleburgh, New York, May 11, 2002
items.q: I was doing that for about 18 years with Harvey Swartz

ctx.x: Great. When you look at your career as a musician, what’s happening right now, do you feel it’s a good place for you? © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-

This is the best time in my life right now. I can’t believe what’s happened to me. I mean I’m going to be 74 in November, and what has happened to me every year has become more and more and more. Between going away and doing like workshops in other countries and concerts, being able to re-establish the bass and voice again, I was doing that for about 18 years with Harvey Swartz and then he felt he didn’t want to do it anymore which was fine, you know, he’s a wonderful musician. But I didn’t want to let it go.…
Was it a conscious thing at that time? I mean sometimes those things — I’ve heard stories about well this saxophone, this bass thing happened simply because the other people didn’t show up.
